question_text: a. i. Identify the topologies labelled A, B, C and D A - Hybrid topology B - Tree topology C - Ring topology D - Dual ring topology             1 mark each × 4 = 4 marks ii. State one feature each of the diagrams labelled above. A - Hybrid Topology * Combination: Utilizes a mixture of two or more different network topologies. * Scalability: Offers flexibility for expansion and adaptation to varying network requirements. * Reliability: Provides redundancy and fault tolerance by incorporating multiple topology structures. * Complexity: Can be more complex to design, implement, and manage compared to single- topology networks. B - Tree Topology: * Hierarchy: Organized in a hierarchical structure with a root node at the top and branches extending downward. * Centralization: Features a central node (root) that controls the flow of communication. * Scalability: Supports expansion by adding more branches or nodes to the existing structure. * Dependency: Relies heavily on the central node, making it vulnerable to single point of failure. C - Ring Topology: * Ring Structure: Nodes are connected in a circular arrangement, where each node is connected to exactly two other nodes. * Token Passing: Utilizes token passing mechanism for data transmission, where only the node with the token can send data. * Simple Configuration: Relatively simple to configure and implement compared to other topologies. * Failure Impact: Susceptible to network disruption if any node or connection in the ring fails, causing the entire network to be affected. D - Dual Ring Topology: * Redundancy: Features two interconnected rings, providing redundancy and fault tolerance. * Data Transmission: Utilizes one ring for data transmission while the other serves as a backup. * Increased Reliability: Offers increased reliability compared to a single ring topology due to redundancy. * Complexity: Can be more complex to implement and manage compared to single-ring topologies due to dual infrastructure. 1 mark each × any 4 = 4 marks b. i.
